questions.title: Between the greater and lesser wings of the sphenoid
questions.question: Which anatomical structure passes exactly between the greater and the lesser wings of the sphenoid bone?

options.A: The narrow inferior orbital fissure opening
options.C: The completely circular optic canal opening
options.D: The deep and hidden pterygomaxillary fissure

explanations.A: Incorrect. The inferior orbital fissure lies between the sphenoid's greater wing and the maxilla — a different pair of bones from the sphenoid's own two wings.
explanations.B: Correct. The superior orbital fissure is the gap between the greater and lesser wings of the sphenoid bone, opening into the back of the orbit. It transmits the nerves of eye movement and sensation — the oculomotor, trochlear, ophthalmic division of the trigeminal, and abducens nerves — along with the superior ophthalmic vein. Its location, specifically between the two sphenoid wings, is what this question isolates.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The optic canal is a separate, more medial opening within the lesser wing alone, carrying only the optic nerve and ophthalmic artery — not a passage between the two wings.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The pterygomaxillary fissure lies between the pterygoid process of the sphenoid and the maxilla, connecting the pterygopalatine fossa to the infratemporal fossa — a different location from the gap between the sphenoid's own two wings.

questions.learning_objective: Locate the superior orbital fissure between the greater and lesser wings of the sphenoid.
